title: All six internal-token-secured microservices boot with their expected internal secret configured (no silent 503 on internal routes)
description: notification-internal.routes.js, risk-management-service's internal.routes.ts, and trust-vault-service's s2s.routes.ts all return 503 'not configured' when their respective env var (INTERNAL_API_TOKEN/INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN/INTERNAL_API_KEY) is unset — a fast smoke check to run right after any deployment/config change.
steps: After deploying/restarting vibrantix-backend, vendor-service, risk-management-service, trust-vault-service, vciso-service, assistant-service, and connector-service, call one lightweight internal endpoint on each with a valid shared token
Confirm none return 503 'Internal endpoint not configured' / 'S2S token not configured'
expectedResult: Every service's internal-token-secured route responds normally (200/401 depending on token correctness) — none respond 503 due to a missing internal secret env var post-deploy.

title: BACKEND_URL and INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN are configured on every microservice that depends on the shared entitlement/project-scope clients
description: entitlement-client.cjs and project-scope-client.cjs both fall back to a placeholder 'https://billing.internal:5000' baseURL that never resolves in any real environment when neither ENTITLEMENT_BASE_URL nor BACKEND_URL is set. A missing config here fails closed (503) rather than crashing loudly, which means this misconfiguration can go unnoticed until a user hits a permission/entitlement check.
steps: On each of vendor-service, risk-management-service, trust-vault-service, connector-service, vciso-service, assistant-service, confirm BACKEND_URL (or ENTITLEMENT_BASE_URL) and INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN are present in the running environment
Perform one action per service that exercises getScope() or resolve() (e.g. any permission-gated action)
expectedResult: No service silently falls back to the 'billing.internal:5000' placeholder host — every project-scope/entitlement lookup resolves against the real backend URL, and no user-facing action fails with a generic 503 caused by this misconfiguration.

title: audit-report-generator-service is reachable from vibrantix-backend at the configured AUDIT_REPORT_SERVICE_URL
description: auditReportService.js defaults to http://localhost:8005 when AUDIT_REPORT_SERVICE_URL is unset, which — like the AI policy service's port-8002 default — will not resolve inside a containerized deployment and silently breaks all report generation for every audit in every org.
steps: Confirm AUDIT_REPORT_SERVICE_URL is set to the actual service address in the current environment
From /audit-assurance, trigger report generation for any completed audit
Confirm the job is accepted (not an immediate connection-refused error)
expectedResult: Report generation is accepted and progresses past job submission — no ECONNREFUSED/502 caused by AUDIT_REPORT_SERVICE_URL defaulting to an unreachable localhost port.

title: Core cross-service list/detail endpoints return the documented 'success' + 'data' envelope shape consistently
description: Across the codebase the convention is a top-level { success: boolean, data: {...} } (or { success, error } on failure) envelope — seen consistently in notification-internal.routes.js, s2s.routes.ts, and RiskManagementApiClient's expectations ({ success, data }). A service that deviates (e.g. returns the payload unwrapped, or uses 'result' instead of 'data') breaks every typed consumer silently at the type level.
steps: Spot-check one representative endpoint from each of vibrantix-backend, vendor-service, risk-management-service, trust-vault-service for its top-level JSON response envelope on both success and error paths
expectedResult: Every checked endpoint uses the { success, data } / { success, error } envelope shape — no endpoint silently renames 'data' to 'result'/'payload' or omits 'success' entirely.
